lines: Namaste, I'm Hema. You're watching This Day, That Year.
Today's date is the fifth of October. And fifteen years ago, it was 2026.
Ancient banking. HDFC Bank named Anup Bagchi its first external managing director and CEO, starting the twenty-seventh of October. A new chair, same queue.
Early cloud. Google's Project Suncatcher prototype rode a Falcon 9 to test AI chips in orbit. In 2041 the cloud is literally a cloud.
Vintage cars. India notified CAFE-III norms, aiming for a sixteen point seven percent fuel efficiency gain by twenty thirty two. Petrol was still a personality then.
Old sport. India finished fourth at the Asian Games with eighty-five medals, twenty-one of them gold.
Fifteen years on, the chips have gone to space and the traffic has not moved.
That's the record. Everything else is just a take. I'm Hema. Namaste, see you at the next bulletin.
Namaskara! Meter down. Tchu Tchu reporting, live from the taxi.
A banker hailed me and said his bank has a new boss. I said the Padmini has had the same boss for fifty years. The meter is still running.
Google is testing chips in space. My chips are tested at the Shivajinagar stall, and they are never ready. Work is warship.
Eleventh notice from Fa King Construction at Celeb Shauchalay. It arrived by drone again. The Dalmatian chased the drone. Something is fishy with the Dalmatian.
Tchu Tchu, AIMTV, Bombai. The meter is still running.
Hi guys! It's Stomach Challo, and I have left the country once more. Same shoes, new accent. I love foreign.
Okay, it is Lonavala. But the hills are so green and the fog is so Scottish. Edinburgh called, and I let it go to voicemail.
I tried the famous chikki. In Europe they call it a nut bar with a story. Here it comes in a paper bag and a lot of confidence.
There is a long queue for vada pav at the viewpoint. In Paris, it is called a line for the Louvre. Same patience, less glass.
The monsoon just left early, so the waterfalls are on a break. Very union, very Switzerland. Even the water takes weekends.
That's it for today. Stay hungry, stay foreign. This is Stomach Challo, signing off from West India.
Namaste, Juhu Chaiwala here. Welcome to Tomorrow Shop. Products from the future, delivered to the footpath.
Today's product is the Rupee Umbrella. A tiny umbrella that opens whenever it rains dollars, so your rupee stays dry.
Fifteen years ago the reserves dropped by eighteen billion in a week. We did not panic. We made an umbrella.
At the sunny entrance, the Rupee Umbrella costs Rs 7,500 and comes with a gold handle. At the shadow entrance, it costs Rs 120 and comes with a handle.
It folds to the size of a coin, which is useful, because that is all you will have left.
You can pay in chai. Chai is Rs 12 at the shadow entrance and Rs 900 at the sunny entrance. Choose your weather carefully.
Here is your chai. From a bot.
Short of money and long on dreams? Try Fa Loan, the loan that lends you confidence.
Approval in one blessing. Interest paid in advice, mostly unsolicited.
Fa Loan starts at Rs 999 a month. Side effects may include eviction.
Fa Corp. We lend what you borrow.
Namaste. Sindhi Crawford here, Road Cross, since two thousand eight. The monsoon is leaving, but the puddles are not.
Hot and humid means slow walkers and quick drivers. Look both ways, then look again. A zebra crossing is a suggestion only if you are a zebra.
Don't take tension. We help you cross.
Baa baa. Today's blessing: may your chai be warm, your queue be short, and your notice be unread.
